summary.tldr: Creates a new federal digital safety law and commission to regulate some online services, especially to reduce harmful content and protect children.
what_it_does: Requires regulated social media and chatbot services to take steps to reduce harmful content, including blocking tools, flagging tools, content labels and crisis intervention for chatbots.
Requires operators of regulated services to protect children, including age checks for pornographic content and, for some social media services, steps to stop under 16s from opening accounts.
Requires regulated social media services to remove, in some cases, child sexual abuse material and intimate images shared without consent, with a complaint process to the new commission.
Creates the Digital Safety Commission of Canada to oversee the law, handle complaints, issue guidelines, inspect operators and order compliance.
Requires operators to file public digital safety plans that explain their measures, resources and moderation practices, with limits on personal information and some confidential details.
summary.background: The bill enacts the Digital Safety Act and the Digital Safety Commission of Canada Act. It also makes related changes to other Acts.
